Area check: Cliopatria 2,169 km2 against the Rhodes infobox 1,400.68 km2 (ratio 1.55, within a factor of two: the shape includes the offshore cells and islets around the island). 'Lord of Rhodes and the Cyclades' is Leo's title in the August 1234 treaty with Venice, but the Cyclades were the Duchy of the Archipelago's; the page names no other island of the domain, so only Rhodes is drawn.

correction.text: shape unchanged (the island of Rhodes), but Gabalas rule holds only to 1248; the Genoese hold the island 1248-1250 and it is a Nicaean province from 1250

keyframe_review.note: Years: 'occupied by the Genoese in 1248-1250' (Rhodes page); the Leo Gabalas page: 'The Genoese seized the island' in 1248 and Gabalas rule ended formally 'probably after the final eviction of the Genoese in 1250'. Cliopatria ends the shape in 1249.

ledger.note: 1204: Rhodes passes to Leo Gabalas. He 'ruled Rhodes and nearby Aegean islands after the Fourth Crusade broke up the Byzantine Empire in 1204'; Rhodes 'had slipped out of imperial Byzantine control' before or during the Fourth Crusade. The page gives no date for his independence (he is 'first securely attested in 1232/3'), so 1204 is the page's year for the break-up and the founding date is a bridge; the Rhodes page: 'the centre of an independent domain under Leo Gabalas and his brother John'.

1248: the Genoese seize Rhodes. John Gabalas called Nicaean troops against a Genoese attack, but 'The Genoese seized the island'; the Rhodes page: 'occupied by the Genoese in 1248-1250'. Hatched, rule 4.

1250: the Genoese are evicted. 'The Genoese were evicted by the Empire of Nicaea' (the Rhodes page gives no year for the eviction; the Genoese occupation is '1248-1250' and the Leo Gabalas page says 'the final eviction of the Genoese in 1250').

1250: the Gabalas domain ends. Gabalas rule 'ended formally soon thereafter, probably after the final eviction of the Genoese in 1250, when the island became a Nicaean province'; the Rhodes page: the island then 'became a province of the Nicaean state' and, after 1261, part of the restored Byzantine Empire.

wars.name: Nicaean expedition against Rhodes
wars.outcome: Vatatzes sent an expedition under Andronikos Palaiologos, supervised by the emperor; 'The island was ravaged, but Leo apparently stayed in effective control'.
wars.note: No ground held, so no contest events. In August 1234 Leo recognised the Doge of Venice as his lord, agreeing mutual assistance against Vatatzes; in 1235/6 he joined Vatatzes' attack on Constantinople (fighting the Venetian fleet): the page's own tension, no border result.

wars.name: Genoese seizure of Rhodes and Nicaean recovery

zones.text: Rhodes, held by the Genoese 1248-1250 until the Nicaeans evicted them

wars.outcome: The Genoese seized the island in 1248 and held it until the Nicaeans evicted them (1250); Rhodes became a Nicaean province and the Gabalas domain ended.
wars.note: Expressed as occupation_start/occupation_end in the ledger, because the Genoese held Domain land without annexing it formally.

certainty.note: An island domain: the coast is its border, but the pages name no other island of the 'Cyclades' and Aegean islands the lord claimed in 1234, so the extent beyond Rhodes is unknown.

notes: Within the 1-2 page budget (two pages). SAME WIKIDATA AS rhodes (Q43048): different states. The 'rhodes' row (Cliopatria 'Rhodes', -188..-165, dossier polities/rhodes.json by another group, dated -408 to -39) is the ancient Rhodian republic; the Domain of Rhodes (1204-1250) is a medieval Gabalas lordship; they share only the island and Wikipedia's 'Rhodes' article, so there are two dossiers. Dates not settled: the independence of the domain (1204 is only the page's year for the break-up of the empire; the Rhodes page does not mention the Fourth Crusade; 'before or during' it); Leo's death ('certainly dead by 1248', year unknown); the Genoese eviction (1250 on the Leo Gabalas page, undated on the Rhodes page); the formal end of Gabalas rule. Suzerainty (no ledger type exists for becoming a vassal; the suzerain's dossier carries it): Leo recognised the Doge of Venice as his lord in August 1234 (republic-of-venice, eu-13, should carry a vassal_start with domain-of-rhodes as counterpart); the page 'surmises' a Nicaean suzerainty at some date (nicaean-empire); the title 'Caesar' may come from Theodore I Laskaris or John III Vatatzes. Byzantine Empire dossier: its 'loss domain-of-rhodes 1314 (Cliopatria drops Rhodes, page silent)' is out of step with these pages: Rhodes was a Nicaean province from 1250, Byzantine after 1261 and Hospitaller by 1306-1310 (Rhodes page: 'in 1306-1310 the island was occupied by the Knights Hospitaller'; a 1305 fief to Andrea Morisco). The Knights Hospitaller (1310-1522) need their own dossier (not in Cliopatria's Domain of Rhodes row). No ruler list entered: no page gives reign years for Leo or John Gabalas. No gazetteer names needed (Rhodes resolves).
